parsed.explanation: The dossier documents a permissive operative regime with no traveler-facing restriction: no criminal statute against trans identity or expression, facility access protected, hate-crime law covering gender identity in force, and documented social acceptance (pride parades with thousands, high public support, a national anti-transphobia day). No border, document, custody, care or police friction against trans visitors is recorded. The sole violence datum — a 2006 killing by youths — is a dated isolated case, weak present-day evidence. The March 2026 roll-back bills pass only first reading and target resident-facing legal gender recognition; they signal political backsliding but do not touch a visitor's home-issued documents, and their final form is unresolved. The ombudsman's un-answered review is an open question, not an exposure. This sits at the 0.85 tier, held below 0.95 by the backsliding trajectory and limited documentation of remedies operating for visitors.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented; no border or passport-marker friction recorded.
entry_documents.protection: Facility access matching gender is protected by law; no entry screening rule targets trans visitors.
entry_documents.interaction: Visitors carry home-issued documents; the roll-back would affect domestic legal gender recognition only, not entry.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Not documented; no arrests, sweeps or custody placement practices recorded.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Hate-crime law treats gender identity as an explicit aggravated-offence ground (Articles 132/144/145).
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Ombudsman's constitutional review of Article 176-C (criminalising 'acts contrary to' gender identity) unresolved; its effect on visitors unknown.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented; no facility bans or birth-sex placement rules recorded.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Access to facilities matching gender is explicitly protected.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Roll-back bills in committee could alter the framework; final form unresolved.

care_services.exposure: Not documented; gender-affirming care is lawful, no visitor refusal cases recorded.
care_services.protection: Care lawful; conversion practices banned since 2024; intersex infant surgery prohibited.
care_services.interaction: Roll-back threatens the intersex-intervention ban and would reintroduce medical opinion for residents' gender change.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: No state threat-framing documented; governing and allied parties advancing roll-back signals political hostility, resident-facing.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Police persecution absent from record; hate-crime aggravation operates.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Differing vote tallies (124/151 to 79) leave the repeal's strength uncertain.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented for visiting minors; school-curriculum 'gender ideology' bills concern resident schooling.
minors_guardians.protection: Self-declaration available from 16 (currently); one opposition bill assessed compatible with school human-rights obligations.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor with an adult faces no distinct documented exposure; curriculum rules would not reach short-stay visitors.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: One dated case: 2006 killing of a trans woman by youths, invoked in 2026 debate; nearly twenty years old, weak present-day signal.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Aggravated-assault hate-crime provision up to four years; public acceptance indicators (pride, high parenting support) documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: No pattern of anti-trans violence, no impunity findings recorded.

remedies_unknowns.protection: Ombudsman institutionally engaged; written parliamentary question on trans health/safety filed.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Review outcome, bill adoption, effective date and correct vote tally all unresolved; committee stage pending.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar tier. Both have explicit equality protections, no traveller-facing restriction, and isolated friction rather than patterns; here the dated 2006 murder parallels 0.85-A's isolated rural stop. The active roll-back movement is the main downward difference.

This scores below. 0.95-A shows operating remedies (audits, ombuds corrections) and complete absence of political threat; here protections are documented but their day-to-day operation for visitors is not, and parliament is actively advancing repeal.

Above. 0.75-C documents actual border screening friction and discretionary detention; this dossier records no visitor-facing friction at all, stronger hate-crime law, and broad documented social acceptance.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime is permissive and visitor-relevant exposures are absent: no criminalisation of presentation, protected facility access, lawful care, and hate-crime aggravation covering gender identity. Social acceptance is documented (mass pride events, top-ranked parenting support, an anti-transphobia national day). The serious negatives are trajectory rather than practice: a first-reading-approved roll-back of self-ID, threat to the intersex-intervention ban, and government-backed parties driving it — all resident-facing measures that would not directly bind a visitor using home documents, but which raise the discovery-severity climate. A single dated (2006) killing and an unresolved Article 176-C review are open questions, not exposures. On balance this sits solidly in Low Risk, just below the 0.95 aspirational tier.
